# LobbyWatch — the rule-buyers of Indian finance, watched

> Independent register of the interests that buy influence over India's financial rules:
> a comment-transparency scorecard for the six statutory consultation desks (RBI, SEBI,
> IRDAI, IBBI, PFRDA, IFSCA), a consultation ledger (were comments published?), an
> interests register (industry bodies, think tanks, foreign lobbies, consumer side), a
> sourced revolving-door ledger, and an RTI playbook with ready-to-file templates.
> Layer 3 (rule-buyers) of the sousveillance stack — RegTrac (rule-writers) and SROTrac
> (rule-borrowers) are layers 1 and 2. Run by CashlessConsumer. Data CC BY 4.0.

Base URL: https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in

## Pages
- [Home](https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in/index.html): comment-transparency scorecard per desk, live consultations, latest door moves.
- [Consultations](https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in/consultations.html): the consultation ledger — opened, closed, status, and whether comments were published.
- [Interests](https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in/interests.html): the interests register — industry bodies, foreign lobbies, think tanks, consumer side, SROTrac layer links.
- [Revolving Doors](https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in/doors.html): documented post-regulator appointments, per person, each with a record link.
- [Access & RTI](https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in/access.html): ready-to-file RTI templates for unpublished comments and committee minutes + the filing log.
- [About](https://lobbywatch.cashlessconsumer.in/about.html): ground rules, roadmap (index scrapers → comments corpus → clause-diff engine), how the stack joins.

## Quick facts
- Consultation desks tracked: 6
- Consultations tracked: 10
- Interests registered: 21
- Documented door moves: 32

## House rule
No insinuation without a paper trail — access and influence are documented through
published comments, RTI replies, minutes and appointment orders, not vibes.

Built 2026-10-05 02:32 UTC.


## index.html

Layer 3 · rule-buyers · the sousveillance stack 
 Who buys the rules of Indian finance? 
 Regulators write the rules; RegTrac watches the writers.
 SROs borrow them; SROTrac watches the borrowers. This register watches
 the buyers : the interests that flood consultations, get the meetings,
 and hire the regulators after retirement. Access and influence are documented through
 published comments, RTI replies, minutes and appointment orders — not vibes. 
 watching the watchers, room three 

 6 consultation desks 
 10 consultations tracked 
 2 open for comments 
 21 interests registered 
 32 documented door moves 

 Comment-transparency scorecard 
 The first test of a captured consultation is whether anyone can see what was said to
the rule-writer. Stance per desk, as verified on the regulator's own site. 

 Desk Statute Publishes comments? Documented practice 

 Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India 
 Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016 
 yes 
 Runs a Public Comments section; its discussion papers instruct commenters to submit through the website with stakeholder categories, and comments are published there. 
 source 

 International Financial Services Centres Authority 
 IFSCA Act 2019 
 unknown 
 Consultation papers listed on ifsca.gov.in. Whether comments received are published is unverified — flagged for checking. 
 source 

 Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India 
 IRDA Act 1999 
 unknown 
 Consultation papers published on its portal. In June 2026 IRDAI proposed a formal regulation-making framework: minimum 21-day public comment window and a general statement of response to comments published by the date regulations are notified. Until notified, publication of comments is not a settled practice. 
 source 

 Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority 
 PFRDA Act 2013 
 unknown 
 Consultation papers published on the site (e.g. Sept 2025 valuation-alignment paper via PIB). Whether comments received are published is unverified — flagged for checking. 
 source 

 Reserve Bank of India 
 Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 
 no 
 No general practice of publishing comments received on discussion papers. Commenters self-publish instead (NASSCOM posted its own submission on the Charges paper; Vidhi posted its 2019 PA/PG submission). Individual comment-archives exist only because commenters chose to publish. RTI is the fallback route. 
 source 

 Securities and Exchange Board of India 
 SEBI Act 1992 
 yes 
 Posts consultation papers and the comments received on its public-comments portal; a board-approved procedure (18 Dec 2024) formalised pre-legislative consultation for regulation-making. 
 source 
 Why the person paying should care: 
when comments are secret, you cannot tell whether a rule was rewritten for the industry
that asked — or tested against the public that pays. RBI's 2022 Charges-in-Payment-Systems
paper drew submissions from every major industry body; none were published, and the
commenters had to self-publish. A rule made in a closed room still lands on your bill.  SEBI (Procedure for Making, Amending and Reviewing of Regulations) — formalised pre-legislative consultation Board-approved procedure (18 Dec 2024) making structured pre-legislative consultation mandatory — the strongest transparency baseline among the six desks; the watch compares other regulators against it.

 03 Oct 2022 
 Discussion Paper on Charges in Payment Systems (40 questions on UPI/IMPS/NEFT/card charges) Submissions were never published by RBI; commenters self-published (NASSCOM's full submission is public by its own choice). The paper set off the UPI-charges debate; the finance ministry publicly denied any plan to charge UPI, and the merchant-discount-rate question resurfaced in later rule-making.

 RBI 
 final 
 no source 
 How to read this table: 
"unknown" is a finding, not a gap in this register — it means the regulator has not
demonstrated a practice of publishing what it receives. RTI is the fallback route;
see Access & RTI for ready-to-file templates.

## interests.html

the interests register 
 Who is in the room 
 The organised interests that seek to shape India's financial policy —
industry bodies, think tanks, foreign lobbies, and (for balance) the consumer side.
Every entry is a fact of existence and a public role; positions are recorded only where
documented.

 IT-industry body; self-published its feedback on RBI's Charges-in-Payment-Systems discussion paper (Oct 2022), arguing that zero or low fees can deter innovation and competition — a documented position on the UPI pricing question.

 Payments Council of India 
 payments 
 Apex payments-industry council formed in 2013 under the aegis of IAMAI; self-describes as representing 90%+ of the payments industry; runs committees (merchant aggregators & acquirers, payment processors, networks) and publishes policy-position pages on regulation. 
 site · source

 Policy foundation working on digital-economy issues incl. payments and platform regulation; files submissions and op-eds in regulatory debates.

 Research institution focused on financial-systems design for low-income households; publishes on customer-protection architecture in payments and credit.

 Layer discipline: RBI-recognised
SROs keep their rosters in SROTrac 
(rule-borrowers). They appear here only as layer links — the same institutions also
lobby directly, which is exactly why the two layers are cross-referenced.

## doors.html

the revolving-door ledger 
 From the regulator's chair to the board's 
 Documented post-office moves of financial regulators into the boards of
the entities they regulated — and the bodies that set their industry's codes. Every row
is an appointment order, an exchange filing or a credible press record. Where an
appointment required the former employer's approval, that fact is stated.

 What this ledger is not: it is not
an accusation of wrongdoing, and no row implies a quid pro quo. It is the factual
substrate for the capture question: who moved, when, to whom, with whose approval.
Interpret it; don't outsouce interpretation to us.

## access.html

access & RTI 
 Ask what they won't publish 
 Where a regulator does not publish consultation comments or minutes,
the Right to Information Act is the fallback. These are ready-to-file templates and the
running log of what this desk has asked and received. File at
 rtionline.gov.in (₹10; first copy
of pages free). 
 Template 1 — comments on a consultation RTI Template — Comments received on a consultation paper 
 To: The Central Public Information Officer, <REGULATOR NAME AND ADDRESS> 
 Subject: Information sought under Section 6(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 
 Why this template exists: regulators invite "public comments", but several — 
 RBI above all — do not publish what they receive. The consultation record is 
 the raw material of policy capture analysis. Section 2(f) of the RTI Act 
 covers "information held in any material form"; received comments are held 
 information. Precedent: comments on RBI's Discussion Paper on Charges in 
 Payment Systems (2022) were never published; commenters had to self-publish 
 (NASSCOM, Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy). 
 I request copies of the following information held by your public authority: 
 1. Copies of all comments/feedback/responses received on 
 **[PAPER TITLE AND NUMBER, e.g. "Discussion Paper on Charges in Payment 
 Systems dated 17 August 2022"]**, in any format (email, letter, PDF, 
 portal upload), including those received after the stated deadline. 
 2. A list of all persons/organisations that submitted such comments, with 
 the date of each submission and the mode of submission. 
 3. If any comments were not considered or were excluded, the reason recorded 
 for each such exclusion. 
 4. Copies of any "action taken"/response statement, presentation, or 
 internal note summarising the comments received and the changes made to 
 the draft in response. 
 Period to which the information relates: **[DATES, e.g. 17 August 2022 to 31 December 2022]**. 
 If the information is held by another public authority, kindly transfer this 
 application under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005, and inform me of the 
 transfer. 
 Application fee of Rs 10 is remitted herewith / by IPO no. **[NUMBER]** / 
 online. I am a citizen of India. 
 Name: **[NAME]** 
 Address for correspondence: **[ADDRESS]** 
 Phone/Email: **[CONTACT]** 
 --- 
 **Filing notes** 

 File online at [rtionline.gov.in](https://rtionline.gov.in) against the 
 regulator's public authority (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, IBBI and IFSCA are 
 all listed). 
 Expected first response: 30 days. First appeal: Section 19(1) within 30 
 days of non-response or unsatisfactory response. 
 **Log every filing in `data/rti_log.csv`** — the log is published on the 
 Access page. A disclosure that never reaches the public record serves only 
 the filer. 
 Template 2 — committee minutes RTI Template — Minutes of meetings between the regulator and industry 
 To: The Central Public Information Officer, <REGULATOR NAME AND ADDRESS> 
 Subject: Information sought under Section 6(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 
 Why this template exists: the strongest documented form of lobbying access 
 is the meeting minute. Committee meeting minutes, visitor records and 
 agenda papers are "information" under Section 2(f). Pair this template 
 with the comments-disclosure template to connect *who was heard* with 
 *what they asked for*. 
 I request copies of the following information held by your public authority: 
 1. Copies of minutes, agenda papers and attendance records of all meetings 
 of **[COMMITTEE NAME, e.g. "the Advisory Committee on Payment and 
 Settlement Systems" / "the committee constituted to examine [SUBJECT]"]** 
 held between **[START DATE]** and **[END DATE]**. 
 2. Copies of any notes, submissions or presentations made to the committee 
 by industry associations, member institutions or their representatives. 
 3. The list of members of the said committee with their designation and 
 the organisation they represent. 
 4. Copies of visitor/guest entries recorded for meetings between officials 
 of your authority and representatives of **[ASSOCIATION OR COMPANY]** on 
 **[DATES OR DATE RANGE]**, if such records are maintained. 
 Period to which the information relates: **[DATE RANGE]**. 
 If any part of the requested records is exempt, kindly sever only the exempt 
 portion and provide the remainder, as required by Section 10 of the RTI Act, 
 2005, along with the specific exemption invoked. 
 If the information is held by another public authority, kindly transfer this 
 application under Section 6(3) and inform me of the transfer. 
 Application fee of Rs 10 is remitted herewith / by IPO no. **[NUMBER]** / 
 online. I am a citizen of India. 
 Name: **[NAME]** 
 Address for correspondence: **[ADDRESS]** 
 Phone/Email: **[CONTACT]** 
 --- 
 **Filing notes** 

 File online at [rtionline.gov.in](https://rtionline.gov.in). 
 Partial disclosure under Section 10 is common; the fact that a meeting 
 happened, who attended and the final minutes are rarely exempt — push back 
 on blanket refusals via first appeal. 
 **Log every filing in `data/rti_log.csv`.** 
 Filed by this desk Filed Authority Subject Status Outcome Multiple (per consultation) Comments received on a named consultation paper + response statement template-ready Multiple (RBI desks first) Minutes of committee meetings where industry bodies were heard template-ready House rule: this log fills only
with filings actually made. A template waiting to be filed is marked as such — we don't
claim RTI victories we haven't fought.

## about.html

methodology 
 About LobbyWatch 
 LobbyWatch is the third layer of India's financial-policy
 sousveillance stack . Surveillance is watching citizens; sousveillance
is citizens watching back. Room one (rule-writers) is watched by
 RegTrac ; room two (rule-borrowers) by
 SROTrac ; this register watches room
three — the rule-buyers. 

 Ground rules 

 Public data first — statutes, gazettes, published comments, regulator websites, press of record. 
 Every claim sourced per row — with dates. If a figure has no source, it stays out. 
 "As of" stamped everywhere — corrections are visible, never silent. 
 Consumer payoff required — every page answers "why should the person paying care". 
 No insinuation without a paper trail — access and influence are documented through meetings, minutes, comment letters and appointment orders, not vibes. 

 What is in the register today 

 consultation desks scored 6 
 consultations tracked 10 
 interests registered 21 
 documented door moves 32 

 The roadmap (build order from SOUSVEILLANCE.md) 

 Done — consultation ledger. Cross-regulator ledger with the comments-published fact (this release). 
 Done — interests register. Industry bodies, think tanks, foreign lobbies, consumer side (this release). 
 Done — revolving-door ledger. Sourced post-office appointments (this release). 
 Done — RTI playbook. Ready-to-file templates + filing log (this release). 
 Next — consultation-index scrapers. Automated refresh of RBI/SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA/IBBI/IFSCA consultation indexes (formats vary wildly). 
 Next — comments corpus. Download published comments at scale; file RTIs for the unpublished ones. 
 Then — the diff engine. Draft clause → final clause → which commenter's language appears in the rule. 

 How the layers join 

 RegTrac ↔ LobbyWatch 
 Appointment authorities (Appointments Committee of the Cabinet; Financial Sector
Regulatory Appointments Search Committee) are RegTrac rows. The revolving door lands
people from this layer into room one. 

 SROTrac ↔ LobbyWatch 
 SRO members are the same institutions that flood consultation processes. A rule that
survives consultation unchanged toward industry comments is a LobbyWatch finding; the
membership that wanted it is a SROTrac fact. 

 Data & code 
 Everything is CSV-first in the open repo ( GitHub );
HTML is generated from the CSVs. Data licensed CC BY 4.0 (attribute
"LobbyWatch / CashlessConsumer"); code MIT. Agent entry point:
 llms.txt .

 The Sousveillance Stack — who writes, borrows and buys the rules 

 Layer 1 · rule-writers RegTrac India's statutory financial regulators live 
 Layer 2 · rule-borrowers SROTrac India's financial-sector self-regulatory organisations live 
 Layer 3 · rule-buyers LobbyWatch consultations, access, revolving doors you are here 

 LobbyWatch — an independent CashlessConsumer project tracking who buys influence over India's financial rules: consultation records, meeting access and revolving doors. Not affiliated with any regulator, association or company; every claim is sourced per entry. 
 Layer 3 of the sousveillance stack: RegTrac (rule-writers) · SROTrac (rule-borrowers) · LobbyWatch (rule-buyers). 
 cashlessconsumer.in · data & code: GitHub · methodology · llms.txt
